skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations - manage active and reactive communication - support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders
You can: - understand the appropriate media to communicate findings - shape communications for the audience
You can: - undertake data profiling and source system analysis - present clear insights to colleagues to support the end use of the data

You can: - evolve and define data governance - take responsibility for supporting and collaborating around wider governance - assure and integrate data services to meet the needs of multiple business services - work proactively to ensure the organisation designs architecture that considers data

You can: - experiment with unfamiliar and emerging technologies, or familiar technologies in new data contexts, with guidance - share what you learn with the team, explaining potential benefits, risks, and practical considerations - identify opportunities to apply technology to improve data processes or outcomes in an operational setting or the wider organisation

You can: - produce relevant data models across multiple subject areas - explain which models to use for which purpose - understand industry-recognised data modelling patterns and standards, and when to apply them - compare and align different data models

You can: - create data standards for different subjects and ensure senior leaders understand them - work with subject matter experts across the organisation to introduce data standards best practice - monitor compliance with policies and standards in the organisation - make recommendations about how the organisation should resolve breaches of standards

You can: - design an appropriate metadata repository - suggest changes to improve current metadata repositories - understand a range of tools for storing and working with metadata - advise less experienced members of the team about metadata management
You can: - ensure that the right actions are taken to investigate, resolve and anticipate problems - co-ordinate the team to investigate problems, implement solutions and take preventive measures
You can: - work within a strategic context and communicate how activities meet strategic goals - contribute to the development of strategy and policies

skill: Turning business problems into data design
expected_level_description: You can: - design data architecture that deals with problems spanning different business areas - identify links between problems to devise common solutions - work across multiple subject areas, or a single large or complicated subject area - produce appropriate patterns

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload

You can: - design data models and reference sets using clinical terminologies - map between terminologies and classifications, and explain the limits of a mapping - advise teams on terminology use in products and analytics

You can: - design and build integrations using FHIR, HL7 version 2, and messaging patterns - write and profile FHIR resources and implementation guides - resolve complex mapping and data quality issues between systems

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - define data quality rules and measures - work with data providers to fix the root causes of poor quality
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - supervise day-to-day work and give feedback - take part in recruitment and induction - hold regular one-to-one conversations
